theme: 3 terms on hiding types: a return type that hides one real type, a box for any conforming type, and wrapping types in one common type

terms.definition: A return type written with `some` that hides the real type but keeps it the same every time.
terms.example: `body` returns an Opaque Type, so we never write the long view type.

terms.definition: A type written with `any` that can hold a value of any type that conforms to a protocol.
terms.example: The array needs an Existential Type because it mixes squares and dots.

terms.definition: A technique that wraps different concrete types in one common type so they can be used the same way.
terms.example: `AnyHashable` uses Type Erasure, so one set can hold an `Int` and a `String`.
terms.code:
let a: AnyHashable = 1
let b: AnyHashable = "one"
let set: Set<AnyHashable> = [a, b]
print(set.count)

Today's terms
Opaque Type - A return type written with `some` that hides the real type but keeps it the same every time.
Existential Type - A type written with `any` that can hold a value of any type that conforms to a protocol.
Type Erasure - A technique that wraps different concrete types in one common type so they can be used the same way.

landscape.hook: Can you explain some and any in English?

dialogue.title: some or any?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why does `makeIcon` return `some Shape` and not just `Square`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's an Opaque Type. Callers know it's a `Shape`, but not which one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can it return a different shape next time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. An Opaque Type always hides the same real type.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then how does `all` hold different shapes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: `any Shape` is an Existential Type. It's a box for any `Shape`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So an Existential Type is like Type Erasure?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Kind of. `any` does Type Erasure for you, with no wrapper to write.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Before `any`, we wrote wrappers like `AnyShape` by hand, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, that was manual Type Erasure. Now use `some` first, `any` when types differ.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Opaque Type for one hidden type, Existential Type for a mixed list.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's an Opaque Type. One hidden real type.
